..(Thursday night through Tuesday)
Issued at 400 AM EDT WED AUG 26 2026

The most current model data continues to suggest the increasing
influence of the southern upper-level ridge into Kentucky over 
the weekend. Ahead of this, though, we still see the potential for
a few showers and thunderstorms on Friday owing to a secondary
cold front slowly pressing through eastern Kentucky and exiting 
the state that night. Dry conditions and another warming trend
follows later in the weekend and beyond. 

The previous long term discussion follows:

The period is expected to begin with an upper level ridge centered
in the southwest Conus with the axis of the ridge extending to MT
and Manitoba while an upper level low should be centered over
Hudson Bay to the eastern Great Lakes to eastern KY to the
Southeast. Well to the west, an upper level trough should be
nearing the BC coast to the west coast of the Conus. At the 
surface, an area of low pressure should be centered near the 
Ontario and Quebec border with a cold front trailing into the 
Lower OH Valley to the Southern Plains. A ridge of sfc high 
pressure should extend from Manitoba to the Northern to Central 
Plains to mid MS Valley.

Thursday to Friday night, the upper level low in Canada should
move into northern Quebec, while the associated trough should 
move into western Quebec to the mid Atlantic states to Southeast. 
At the same time, the upper ridge centered in the Southwest Conus
should become centered over southern NM while the axis of the 
ridge tot he north moves to Manitoba to the Dakotas to Co while 
this ridge also builds east into the Lower MS Valley and the Lower
OH Valley and TN Valley. At the same time, the the upper level
trough initially nearing the west coast of Canada and the western
Conus should move into western Canada to Northwest Conus. The sfc
low in advance of the upper trough in sections of eastern Canada
to the eastern Conus, should track into Quebec to the Maritimes
with the trailing cold front crossing eastern KY late Thursday
evening into Thursday night. A secondary boundary passes the area
in more of a dry manner later Friday into Friday night with a sfc
ridge building across the Great Lakes to Lower OH Valley in its
wake. Recent guidance suggests 1500 to 2500 J/kg of MLCAPE for
Thursday afternoon and evening with 20 to 30KT of bulk shear. This
moderate instability and modest shear values could support some
organized line segments capable of strong to locally damaging
wind gusts. Recent EC based AI/machine learning guidance also 
support some lower probabilities of Convective Hazards along with 
GEFS based probabilties also elevated for that timeframe.

Saturday to Sunday night, upper ridging should become centered 
over the mid MS Valley southwest to the Southern Plains from 
Saturday to Saturday night and then over the Southeastern Conus 
through Sunday into Sunday night. The upper trough initially
extending into the Mid Atlantic states shifts to the northeast 
and to the Maritimes while the upper trough initially over 
western Canada to the Northwest moves east to Manitoba to the 
Northern and Central Plains. A ridge of sfc high pressure 
initially from the eastern Great Lakes to Lower OH Valley 
gradually shifts off the Northeast U.S Coast to the Southern 
Appalachians and become centered over the Southern Plains by late 
Sunday night. Further west and northwest an area of low pressure 
should trek near the US Canadian border with a warm front lifting 
toward the Lower OH Valley late Sunday into Sunday night. This 
scenario would favor mainly dry weather with the potential for 
moderate ridge/valley splits with highs near normal to as much as 
5 degrees above normal. 

Monday to Tuesday, upper level ridging should extend from the
Southern Plains across the Southern Plains to portions of the
Atlantic. The shortwave moving from Manitoba to Ontario and near
the Quebec border and also crossing the Great Lakes and into the
Mid Atlantic/Northeast. The associated sfc system should pass well
to the north while a frontal zone/baroclinic zone should be over
or near eastern KY. Temperatures in the upper 80s to around 90 
and dewpoints in the mid to upper 60s would support marginal to 
moderate instability each afternoon and mainly diurnally driven 
convection.
